run.checkpoint_rule_source: assignments/03-causalbind.md (Notes: score checkpoint_last.pt); CausalBind README 'Evaluation' and DATA.md 'Train/Test Protocol': the paper reports the last checkpoint (epoch 50) of each run; arXiv:2610.07340 Section 4 (p. 8): the main tables report the last checkpoint

problems: conda env create failed on the rented machine: torchsort==0.1.10 is source-only, pip builds it in an isolated env with the latest torch (CUDA 13.0), and with the image's nvcc 11.8 on the path it also builds a CUDA kernel, which torch refuses (CUDA version mismatch). The A1 machine has no CUDA toolkit, so it built only the CPU extension there. /usr/local/cuda was moved aside for that one command, giving the same build; environment.yml and code/changes.diff are unchanged
Miniforge is installed from releases/latest, which moved from conda 26.7.2 (A1) to 26.9.4 (A3); the environment itself is pinned and came out the same
Uni-Core's python setup.py install fetches the newest setuptools as an egg: 84.2.1 here, 84.0.0 at A1; the active setuptools is 75.8.0 in both

PairDataset reads DATA_DIR/cache/{mol_smi2idx,pocket_name2idx}_train_blend.json, but download_data.sh saves the released copies in data/; without them the first run rebuilds both on one CPU core (10.6 min here, before the first update). The rebuilt files are byte-identical to the released ones, so B and C can place the released files in data/cache/

A first version of code/check_index_cache.py looked records up by the key str(idx), as the evaluator's unimol LMDBDataset does, and reported every sample as mismatched; train_task.py uses unicore.data.LMDBDataset, which indexes in LMDB key order. Corrected in commit d834484; the corrected check and a byte comparison with the rebuilt files both pass
Each training checkpoint is 3.16 GB (it holds the optimizer state). scripts/train.sh keeps every epoch (--keep-last-epochs 50) and up to 8 best checkpoints, about 190 GB per 50-epoch run

Scoring the 3.16 GB smoke checkpoint on DEKOIS took 4.7 min on the A100 against 2.7 min for the 0.57 GB released checkpoint on the RTX 3060; not investigated (load time and the live UniProt fetch on a fresh machine are both included)

Checkpoint A total is about 2.7 GPU-hours (A2 1.48 on the RTX 3060, A3 1.2 on the A100), over the 1 GPU-hour budget; of the A3 hour, GPU compute was under 6 minutes (training 20 s, reload scoring 4.7 min), the rest environment build, downloads and the index rebuild
